stable.notes:
### Added
- **Agent-readiness: automated write-access inventory (blast radius).** The seat
  audit now reports which non-human actors already write to the portal, counted
  per `hs_object_source_label` via Search: workflow automation, connected apps /
  browser extensions, integrations and direct API. This is the honest blast-radius
  question before an agent joins a portal, "what already has write access here",
  and the gate probe proved the property is filterable so the count is
  recency-independent (sampling recent records gave false negatives -- a portal
  with 10+ enabled workflows read as "no autonomous writers"). New
  `scanners/writesources.py` (`scan_write_sources` -> `WriteSourceScan`), an
  "Agent-readiness: automated write access (blast radius)" section in both report
  formats, and a `scan` echo. Human and human-initiated sources (CRM_UI, IMPORT,
  CLONE_OBJECTS) are excluded. Degrades-and-warns if the object search is
  scope-gated. Verified live on a reference portal: an EXTENSION wrote 571 contacts and
  workflow automation wrote 24 deals. Read-only inventory: it names what writes,
  it does not judge or change any integration.
- **Agent-readiness: workflow collision surface.** The seat audit now reports which
  contact/deal properties enabled workflows already write, so a consultant can say
  "before you point an AI agent at `lifecyclestage`, know 22 workflows already set
  it on a trigger." A workflow and an agent both writing the same field, each on a
  trigger with no human in the loop, is a collision to resolve before connecting the
  agent. The signal rides on the *existing* workflow walk (`automation.py`), so it
  costs zero extra API calls: `measure_sequence_senders` is now `scan_workflows`
  and its `WorkflowScan` carries `property_writes` (property -> the enabled
  workflows that write it), harvested from the verified action keys (`property_name`
  / `target_property` / a `properties` map). Rendered as a new "Agent-readiness:
  workflow collision surface" section in **both the Markdown and HTML** reports and
  echoed by `scan`. Read-only diagnosis: it names the overlap, it does not recommend
  changing any workflow. Verified live on a reference portal (EU1 ENT): 33 properties written
  by 62 enabled workflows, `hubspot_owner_id` (26) and `lifecyclestage` (22) the
  busiest.
- **Shape-drift guard on the workflow scan.** `scan_workflows` walks
  `/automation/v4/flows` to protect sequence-enroll senders from a downgrade
  recommendation. A non-200 already degrades-and-warns, but a **200 with a
  restructured payload** made it return zero senders *silently* -- indistinguishable
  from a portal that simply has no sequence-enroll workflows, so HubScan could
  confidently recommend downgrading a live sender. The scan now checks the shapes
  it reads from (`results` array, per-flow `isEnabled`, the detail `actions` array,
  and the enroll action's `sequenceId` + `senderType` when matched by its known
  id) and sets `SequenceSenderScan.shape_drift`; `scan` warns loudly when it trips.
  This is the guard the P1 v4-deprecation backlog item calls for: HubSpot sunsets
  v4 on 30 Mar 2027, so if a successor API answers 200 with a different structure,
  HubScan now fails visibly instead of quietly dropping sender protection.
- **"Seats never activated" — seats billed to someone who never accepted their
  invite.** These fell through both of the audit's sieves and vanished:
  `count_allocated_seats` counts them (HubSpot bills the slot, the UI shows it
  taken), so they never surfaced as unused *purchased* capacity; and
  `User.is_active` excludes them (they have never logged in), so the activity
  scan never classified them and they never got a recommendation. A seat whose
  holder has provably never logged in is the *strongest* reclaim candidate a
  portal has, and HubScan was silently omitting it. `count_pending_invite_seats`
  + `CostSummary.pending_invite_seats` / `pending_invite_annual` now surface them
  as their own action-item block with a euro figure. Reported **beside** the
  savings total, not inside it: a freshly-sent invite is a legitimately reserved
  seat, and only a human can tell "onboarding" from "abandoned". Found live: 4 of
  8 Service seats on a real portal sat at `invite_pending` — EUR 2,880/yr the
  report never showed.
- **`probe_workflows`** — covers `/automation/v4/flows`, the endpoint the whole
  automation pillar rides on. Nothing probed it before, which is why the bug
  below could hide.
- **`probe_flow_actions` + `probe_object_write_sources`** — two discovery probes
  that answer the feasibility questions behind the agent-readiness signals before
  any scanner is written. `flow-actions` samples enabled flows and enumerates each
  action's `actionTypeId` and field keys, to learn whether an action names the
  property it writes: if it does, a *collision surface* (which workflows already
  write the fields an agent would touch) is buildable at property level; if not,
  the probe prints the real keys so we stop guessing. `object-write-sources`
  answers "what already has write access to this portal", which HubSpot exposes no
  installed-app endpoint for: it observes `hs_object_source_label` /
  `hs_object_source_id` on the most recently modified contacts and deals to
  inventory the integrations actually writing today. Both report their findings
  rather than asserting them. **Run on a reference portal (EU1 ENT, 2026-07-15): both
  signals are buildable.** Flow actions name the property they write via
  `property_name` (set-property), `target_property` (set-owner) or a `properties`
  map (create-record); the probe now recognises all three, so a collision surface
  works at property level. Record source properties yield an actor inventory whose
  live label vocabulary (CRM_UI, IMPORT, EXTENSION, CLONE_OBJECTS,
  AUTOMATION_PLATFORM) is richer than the docs; the probe now flags the autonomous
  writers (incl. `EXTENSION`, a real connected-app writer the first cut missed) and
  collapses per-enrollment id noise. Findings and the full action/label tables are
  in `internal-docs/PROBE_FINDINGS.md`.
- **`probe_source_label_filter`** — the gate probe for the actor-inventory signal.
  A second run (a reference portal, NA1 Pro) showed `object-write-sources`' record sampling is
  unsound: it reported "no autonomous writers" for a portal with 10+ enabled
  property-writing workflows, because the automation writes were older than the
  sample and many records carried no source label at all. The only sound inventory
  counts records *by* source label via Search, which needs `hs_object_source_label`
  to be filterable — not guaranteed for derived source properties. This probe runs
  `HAS_PROPERTY` + per-label `EQ` filters and reports a clean verdict (`200` →
  buildable by count; `400` → not buildable as designed). **Passed on a reference portal
  (EU1 ENT, 2026-07-15): `hs_object_source_label` is filterable.** Counting found
  571 extension-written contacts and 24 automation-written deals portal-wide, where
  the recency sample had seen 5 and 8 — the census the sample can't give. The actor
  inventory is de-risked: a scanner counts records per autonomous source label
  rather than sampling. `object-write-sources` now labels its own output "sample
  only, not a census" so it can't be mistaken for the count.

### Fixed
- **Collision-surface count now pluralises properly** (`6 properties`, not
  `6 propert(ies)`) across the Markdown report, HTML report and `scan` echo.
- **The report no longer claims a Service Hub downgrade is safe.** The
  "Seats to downgrade" block told the client that downgrading "frees the seat
  cost without affecting their work" — an assertion HubScan is not entitled to
  make about a Service Hub seat, because not one of its ten activity signals
  sees a ticket, a conversation, an inbox reply or a chat. A fully-occupied
  Service agent measures as **zero** activity. When the list contains a
  service-hub seat, the block now carries a caveat saying exactly that and asking
  for human confirmation before acting. The failure this prevents is a client
  downgrading a working support team on our say-so. (Now also in
  LIMITATIONS.md, where the Service Hub blind spot was entirely undocumented.)
- **The `automation` scope was missing from HubScan's own scope list.** The
  Workflows API needs the bundled `automation` scope, and
  `automation.sequences.read` does **not** imply it (`403 MISSING_SCOPES` ->
  `requiredGranularScopes: ["automation"]`). It was absent from
  `webapp.REQUIRED_SCOPES` and from PROBE_FINDINGS, so any portal onboarded from
  our own documentation lost the automation pillar — and with it the protection
  that stops HubScan recommending a downgrade for the fixed sender of a live
  sequence-enrolling workflow, which would break that workflow. The scan warned
  ("sequence-sender seats not protected") but `probe` passed clean, so nobody
  looked. Scope added; probe added so it cannot recur.
- **Starter's 5-paid-seat cap is now modelled.** The Nordic Limited Release sells
  Starter with a *maximum of 5 paid seats* (Pro and Enterprise are uncapped). The
  new-pricing model priced any number of Starter seats happily, producing a figure
  HubSpot will not actually sell. `newpricing.new_model_cost` now warns when paid
  seats (Core; free View-Only/Partner seats don't count) exceed
  `STARTER_MAX_PAID_SEATS` and says plainly that Professional is the floor for
  that portal. It deliberately does **not** re-price to Professional — the model
  is analysis-only, and picking the edition is the consultant's call.
- **The Revenue seat no longer resolves to the wrong seat, silently.** The Limited
  Release supplement states the new Front Office seat replaces the legacy Sales,
  Service **and Revenue** seats, but `_OLD_TO_NEW_SEAT` only knew Sales and
  Service — a Revenue-seat holder fell through the unknown-seat default to Core
  (€60/€90 instead of €120/€150), understating the new-model cost with no signal.
  `classify.normalize_seat` now folds `revenue-*` into `revenue-hub` and
  `newpricing.to_new_seat` maps it to Front Office. The raw HubSpot value is
  **inferred, not verified** (no live portal has surfaced a Revenue seat — see
  PROBE_FINDINGS), which is why the fix below matters more than this mapping.
- **Unknown seats are reported instead of quietly costed at zero.** Both sides of
  the old-vs-new comparison silently swallowed a seat they did not recognise:
  `cost.compute_costs` billed it at €0 via `prices.get(seat, 0)`, and
  `newpricing.map_seat_counts` floored it to Core. Either way the headline number
  came out confidently wrong. `CostSummary` now carries `unpriced_seats` (seat ->
  user count) and `map_seat_counts` returns an `unmapped` tuple alongside the
  counts; `scan` warns on both, and the report prints a caveat under the pricing
  table stating that current spend and unused-seat savings are an under-count. A
  mistyped `[<portal>.purchased]` key — previously a silent €0 saving — is caught
  by the same path. The escape hatch is a `[<portal>.prices]` entry.
